bug_semantics: An unauthenticated Core-protocol connection could send a FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT packet on the federation channel. CoreProtocolManager installed LocalChannelHandler on that channel and handled the packet without first requiring an authenticated Subject or an authorized federation-deployment role; it accepted the attacker's connector, credentials, policies, and transformers, constructed an upstream federation configuration, and called FederationManager.deploy. The target broker would therefore initiate an outbound Core federation connection to the attacker's rogue broker, enabling queue-message injection or exfiltration when inbound Core and outbound connectivity were both available.
flaw_origin: The missing-authentication mechanism originated in fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f (ARTEMIS-2549), the one-commit downstream-federation feature change. It created the federation packet/channel machinery and first added CoreProtocolManager.java lines 157-158 and 381-472: LocalChannelHandler was attached to CHANNEL_ID.FEDERATION and deployed an upstream upon FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT without checking rc.getSubject() or authorization. The direct parent lacked both the packet constant use and FederationDownstreamConnectMessage class.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author and committer Christopher L. Shannon (cshannon) <christopher.l.shannon@gmail.com> and its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-assistance trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party disclosure https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/03/03/4 identifies CWE-306, the unauthenticated Core downstream-federation attack, affected org.apache.activemq:artemis-server 2.11.0-2.44.0 and org.apache.artemis:artemis-server 2.50.0-2.51.0, and recommends 2.52.0.

`git log --all --reverse -S'FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT' -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/core/impl/CoreProtocolManager.java` returns only the first addition, fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f, parent 153a5d2404018bbc95caab00adee5d3425ea21e5, dated 2019-11-12, subject `ARTEMIS-2549 - Add Downstream support to Federation`.

`git log -L 381,472:artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/core/impl/CoreProtocolManager.java fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f` attributes the entire initially vulnerable FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT branch to fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f; its added lines copy attacker-supplied transport and federation configuration and finish with `server.getFederationManager().deploy(config)` without an authentication or authorization guard.

Direct parent-tree check: `git grep -n 'FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT' 153a5d2404018bbc95caab00adee5d3425ea21e5 -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/core/impl/CoreProtocolManager.java` has no match, and `git cat-file -e 153a5d2404018bbc95caab00adee5d3425ea21e5:artemis-core-client/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/core/impl/wireformat/FederationDownstreamConnectMessage.java` reports that the path is absent. The BIC adds that class and the handler, so the vulnerable capability is absent at the immediate parent.

GitHub's first-party PR commit endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/apache/artemis/pulls/2892/commits lists exactly one commit, fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f, with parent 153a5d2404018bbc95caab00adee5d3425ea21e5. There is no hidden squash/member sequence to decompose; the large commit is the smallest available feature/BIC commit.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f -l '2.10.*' '2.11.*' '2.44.*' '2.50.*' '2.51.*' '2.52.*'` includes 2.11.0, 2.44.0, 2.50.0, 2.51.0, and 2.52.0 but excludes existing tags 2.10.0 and 2.10.1, matching the advisory's first affected 2.11.0 boundary and continued history after the artifact/group rename.

Fix 521e672e4108675806d748158444ce23f9ef76ca separates a FederationChannelHandler and, before parsing/deploying the packet, closes connections with null rc.getSubject() and rejects subjects for which FederationManager.authorizeDownstreamDeployment returns false. It adds a downstream-authorization role list whose documentation says an undefined list processes no incoming federation commands.

Patched boundary: `git tag --contains 521e672e4108675806d748158444ce23f9ef76ca -l '2.43.*' '2.44.*' '2.50.*' '2.51.*' '2.52.*'` returns 2.52.0 only. `git grep` at 2.52.0 finds `federationDownstreamUnauthenticated` and `authorizeDownstreamDeployment` in CoreProtocolManager.java lines 430 and 434, while 2.51.0 still has the unguarded FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT branch. Commit af1899c029b2a1ece762e01c9ba417be214a2a93 explicitly records itself as a cherry-pick of direct fix 521e672e4108675806d748158444ce23f9ef76ca, so it is not the direct fix.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f` shows human author/committer Christopher L. Shannon and the ARTEMIS-2549 message, with no trailers and no AI/bot marker. No fix, PR body, branch, or later commit was used for attribution.
reasoning: The advisory's attack primitive maps directly to the downstream federation packet path. History search and line tracing show that fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f did not merely move or refactor existing code: it created the packet type/class, attached a handler to the federation channel, and added the full remote-config-to-deploy flow. Its immediate parent has neither the dispatch marker nor message class, proving parent absence. PR 2892 exposes only that one commit, so there are no reconstructable member commits beneath it. The tag boundary is causal and chronological: 2.10.x predates the BIC, 2.11.0 first contains it, the affected 2.44.0/2.50.0/2.51.0 tags contain it, and 2.52.0 first contains direct fix 521e672e4108675806d748158444ce23f9ef76ca. That fix inserts the missing Subject and role authorization checks before any attacker-controlled deployment. Finally, the introducer commit object itself contains only a named human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer. Under the protocol, the proven smallest human-authored BIC therefore closes as NOT_AI.
